page_note: No cosmological substrate present. The entire page is institutional teaching on repentance and forgiveness of sins, distinguishing the catechumen from the Elect, with the Mind of Light dwelling in 'the holy Church.' The page opens with apostolic dialogue frame and proceeds to a sustained ecclesial discourse on the catechumenate, the fast, and the conditions under which prior sins are released. Editorial fatigue score (+20 ecclesial drift in second half) confirms this is a thoroughly institutional unit. The page belongs to the latest pastoral-institutional layer of the Kephalaia.

segments.temporal_note: Pure attribution formula: 'Then said the Apostle to them' — apostolic dialogue frame opening.
Continuation of frame: 'I am the one who reveals it forth to you' — Mani-as-revealer self-attribution.
Opens the institutional teaching: 'every man who has received the hope' — pertaining to the convert/catechumen.
Light/Darkness language used as conversion narrative (the convert separates light from darkness), not as cosmological mapping. Apparatus restoration 'and the faith' confirms ecclesial framing.
'Mysteries of the Living Soul... right hand of Peace' — Manichaean ritual/initiatory language.
'from the Mind of Light who dwells in the holy Church' — explicit ecclesial localization (ⲧⲉⲕⲕⲗⲏⲥⲓⲁ ⲉⲧⲟⲩⲁⲃⲉ).
'holy Church... entreaty of putting-away-of-sin' — institutional sacramental vocabulary.
Continues penitential discourse: 'all his first sins'.
Penitential narrative — sins from birth until conversion.
'received the hope of God' — conversion/initiation language.
'all the doctrines (ⲇⲟⲅⲙⲁ) and idols of Error (ⲡⲗⲁⲛⲏ)' — polemical vocabulary embedded in conversion narrative; ecclesial framing dominates.
'they shall leave them all to him forth' — institutional rule on forgiveness.
'neither shall he receive recompense' — penitential casuistry.
'his living faith' — convert's standing within the community.
Continues the conditional rule on first sins.
Penitential casuistry on the heart's reorientation.
'they shall not pursue them from this moment for any of his first sins' — ecclesial rule on forgiveness.
Conditional clause on apostasy/relapse.
'sin in them another time, then they shall reckon with him' — penitential discipline.
Reckoning of all sins for the relapsed.
'God has given a repentance' — penitential theology.
'putting-away-of-sin (ⲕⲁⲛⲁⲃⲉ)' — Manichaean penitential vocabulary.
'did not strengthen himself in the repentance' — institutional discipline.
Pivots to catechumenate discussion.
'catechumenate (ⲧⲙⲛⲧⲕⲁⲧⲏⲭⲟⲩⲙⲉⲛⲟⲥ) in his faith' — explicit institutional rank.
'they shall release to him forth all his sins' — institutional absolution.
'whether then he is an Elect (ⲉⲕⲗⲉⲕⲧⲟⲥ) in his electate' — explicit Manichaean two-tier institutional structure.
'or a catechumen in his catechumenate' — explicit ecclesial rank.
'this one then who is a catechumen' — institutional category.
'stood firm in the catechumenate' — explicit institutional standing.
Penitential rule on the catechumen's sins.
'on account of his fast (ⲧⲉϩⲛⲏⲥⲧⲓⲁ)' — explicit Manichaean ritual practice as basis for absolution.
